channel.title: DevPulse · Models & training
channel.description: Daily models & training stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: WanPE improves long-form video prompts with shot-level cinematic plans
item.description: The 397B model uses plans built from 1.05M videos and improves human preference by 10.66–18.84 points at 5–15 seconds and 50.86 points at 30 seconds. It is a substantial example of how prompt planning can improve a generative model’s output.

item.title: Shopify turns production failures into daily model updates and cuts serving costs 96%
item.description: Shopify’s continual-learning loop feeds production failures back into model weights daily and reports frontier-model quality with 96% lower serving costs. The case study offers practical lessons for converting user feedback into model improvements while controlling inference spend.

item.title: WROP trains video models on object permanence with 1.5M samples
item.description: WROP provides 150 task designs, a 1.5M-sample corpus, and a 300-question exam; PWM-WROP ranks first among continuation models in a blind Elo study. The released training and evaluation resources make this a useful test of physical reasoning in video models.

item.title: RecCAR aligns cross-modal attention to improve joint video generation
item.description: RecCAR regularizes weaker modality-to-video correspondence toward video-to-modality attention, raising Human Anatomy from 0.69 to 0.75 and reducing audio-video desynchronization from 0.804 to 0.752. The method offers a concrete training intervention for joint video, motion, and audio models.

item.title: RLCD turns reward modeling into calibrated multiway decisions
item.description: RLCD is described as schema-conditioned Plackett–Luce preference modeling with probability calibration, while Jev exposes the reward model through typed outputs and parallel inference. Engineers evaluating model-based decision interfaces can examine how this differs from scalar reward scoring.

item.title: UK AISI uses EvalEval infrastructure to publish reproducible evaluation results
item.description: The UK AI Security Institute is using EvalEval infrastructure to share evaluation results openly, building on a shared schema shaped by prior collaboration. Reproducible reporting makes it easier for engineers to verify and compare model evaluations.

item.title: Jev returns typed probabilistic decisions instead of generated text
item.description: Jev accepts text or structured records and returns numeric outputs for categories, yes/no answers, and ratings with confidence scores; its first model charges $0.042 per million input tokens and nothing for output. This alternative interface and pricing model may suit classification workloads where generated prose is unnecessary.

item.title: Rails keynote argues that LLMs make hand-written code less productive
item.description: The author says DHH framed LLM-generated code as economically preferable for most programmers and questioned whether developers need to read the output. It offers a perspective on how AI coding tools could reshape expectations in a major application framework.

item.title: MentalHealthBench evaluates AI responses to realistic mental health conversations
item.description: The expert-informed benchmark evaluates whether AI responses are helpful and safe in realistic mental health conversations. Engineers building domain-specific assistants can use such evaluations to reason about safety and quality.
